name: Prefab veneers (Snap-On Smile)

lead: Prefab veneers are removable shells worn over the teeth to change how the smile looks: whiter colour, more even shape and masked gaps, visible the moment they go on. They are not bonded and can be taken out, which separates them from dentist-made veneers.
A preformed cover fits over the existing teeth and is held in place by fit rather than bonding. Little published research or encyclopedic coverage addresses removable clip-on veneers specifically.

paras: People buy a kit online, fit the covers over their teeth, and wear them for photos, events or work, taking them out for eating and cleaning. Some use them as a preview before deciding on bonded veneers or other dental work.
No safety or effectiveness studies on removable veneers were found. Information on bonded veneers does not directly apply to them.

angle.text: Users clip on prefab veneers like Snap-On Smile to change the colour, shape or spacing of their front teeth without dentistry, and the change is visible while worn. They are removable, unlike bonded veneers. No research on these removable covers was found.

lead: Prefab or snap-on veneers are removable cosmetic covers marketed to sit over the front teeth to change their apparent colour, shape or spacing without dentistry. They differ from bonded veneers, which are made of composite or porcelain and attached to the tooth, and which are discussed in dental references as thin coverings for discolouration, enamel defects, fractures and shape changes.[1]
Little published research or encyclopedic coverage addresses removable clip-on veneers specifically, so this article is brief.

paras: Dental veneers in the clinical sense are made mainly of composite or dental porcelain and bonded to the tooth; porcelain versions are made indirectly in a laboratory.[1] Reference sources on veneers describe the bonded kinds and do not cover removable clip-on products.[1]
